geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the current flat bar into a more sectionally expressive mass while keeping the dominant gesture and ancestry intact.
Use a folded profile to give the roof/section a clearer public-building character without collapsing into a pure stair-step form.
Keep the long axis reading as the main span direction, consistent with the existing bar logic.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant bar/courtyard gesture, but shift the massing language from a generic cut to a more articulated courtyard condition.
Slightly deepen the void so the public threshold reads more clearly in plan and elevation.
Preserve the verified access-side opening and reinforce the street-facing public response.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently across the four views as a single bar-based mass with one dominant void cut through it. The green parcel is respected; the form sits within it rather than merely filling a bounding box. The blue frontage edge is answered by a clear long-side void/entry seam and a visible ground opening, so the access response is legible rather than sealed. The massing is repairable and not visibly self-colliding. The main weakness is that the silhouette is still basically a rectilinear extrusion with a simple cut, so the section is not yet especially expressive; it is program-plausible for neighborhood living, but not strongly sectional or terrace-driven. The form does not match the more sculptural stepped/tapered references, yet it still aligns enough with the mixed-use/courtyard precedents to pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is taller and more tower-like than the candidate; transfer the profile discipline, not the vertical typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered massing can read as one dominant object with a legible upper profile and clear base relationship.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office-tower scale and proportions are not directly transferable to a compact neighborhood building.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single slender mass with a controlled setback/crown can preserve hierarchy while varying the upper section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is much lower and more storefront-like; only the access/threshold logic is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact street-facing volume with a clear threshold and attached vertical element can support an active ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is less sectional and less continuous; do not copy the big ramped ribbon form, only the void-and-hierarchy principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous sectional idea with a courtyard/void can unify a long bar while giving the ground public usefulness.

warnings: The section reads conservative; if the next iteration wants stronger program character, introduce a more explicit roof/section profile or a clearer inhabited terrace condition.
The void is legible but could become more public or spatially articulated if the brief wants a stronger street threshold.
